Rashi on Sotah 5a:10:1.hebrew: כאשירה - יגדע וישרש אחריה כאשירה, שצריך גידוע אחריה, כדכתיב ואבדתם את שמם (דברים יב):
Rashi on Sotah 5a:10:1.english: Like an Asherah - He will be cut down and uprooted after it, like an Asherah, which requires cutting down after it, as it is written: "And you shall destroy their name" (Deuteronomy 12).

Rashi on Sotah 5a:11:1.english: Shaken off - He awakens at the resurrection of the dead.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:11:2.hebrew: שכבי בעפר לא נאמר - דלישתמע על כל המתים:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:11:2.english: "Lie down in the dust" was not said - so that it would be understood as referring to all the dead.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:11:3.english: Neighbor to dust - He humbles himself to the dust.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:12:2.hebrew: וגבוה ממרחק יידע - רישיה דקרא: כי רם ה' ושפל יראה וגבוה והגבוה ממרחק — מקודם שתבא עליו פורענות ימים רבים — יידע: שכינה מתאוננת ומשתברת עליו. כמו וידע אלמנותיו (יחזקאל יט), ויודע בהם אנשי סכות (שופטים ח), יודע כמביא למעלה (תהלים עד) — לשון שבר:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:12:2.english: And the haughty He knows from afar - The beginning of the verse is: "For the Lord is high, and He sees the lowly," and the haughty, and the haughty one "from afar" — that is, from long before punishment comes upon him, many days earlier — "He knows": the Divine Presence laments and is broken over him. Like "and he knew [i.e., broke] his widows" (Ezekiel 19), "and he made [them] know [i.e., threshed them] with the men of Succoth" (Judges 8), "it is known [i.e., it appears] like one who brings [an axe] upward" (Psalms 74) — an expression of breaking.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:13:1.hebrew: רואה את הגבוה - לקרבו ולהשתדל עמו, וחשוב בעיניו, כמו (הושע ט) "כביכורה בתאנה בראשיתה ראיתי את אבותיכם" — נתתי עיני לקרבם ולחבבם:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:13:1.english: He sees the haughty - to draw him near and to take trouble with him, and he is important in His eyes, as [in] (Hosea 9) "Like the first fruit on a fig tree at its beginning, I saw your fathers" — I set My eyes upon them to draw them near and to hold them dear.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:14:1.hebrew: ואיכא דמתני לה אמספרי לשון הרע - משום רישא דקרא: ״מלשני בסתר רעהו״ וגו':
Rashi on Sotah 5a:14:1.english: And there are those who teach it [the statement] regarding those who speak slander - Because of the beginning of the verse: "One who slanders his neighbor in secret," etc.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:1.hebrew: רוח קימעא עוכרתו - פורענות קלה טורפתו ומאבדתו:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:1.english: A little wind disturbs him - A minor calamity tears him apart and destroys him.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:2.hebrew: והרשעים - גסי הרוח. דקראי דלעיל משתעי בשפלים ונדכאים: "להחיות רוח שפלים וגו'", "כי לא לעולם אריב" עם אותן שפלים, "בעון בצעו וגו'", "דרכיו ראיתי וגו'", "בורא ניב שפתים וגו'". אבל הרשעים, שאינן שפלים ונדכאים — "כים נגרש", כים המגרש ומשליך רפש וטיט לשפתיו סביביו:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:2.english: But the wicked - The arrogant. For the verses above speak of the lowly and the crushed: "To revive the spirit of the lowly, etc."; "For I will not contend forever" with those lowly ones; "For the iniquity of his unjust gain, etc."; "I have seen his ways, etc."; "Creating the fruit of the lips, etc." But the wicked, who are not lowly and crushed — "are like the driven sea": like the sea that casts out and throws up mire and mud onto its shores all around it.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:3.hebrew: כמה רביעיות - לוגי מים. אנו רואים שרוח קימעא עוכרתו, עוכרת את מימיו:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:3.english: How many quarter-[log measures] - [Meaning,] log-measures of water. We see that a little wind stirs it up [and] muddies its waters.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:4.hebrew: אדם שאין בו אלא רביעית אחת - שברביעית דם הוא מתקיים. שיעור זה הלכה למשה מסיני, שרביעית דם מת מטמא באהל, מפני שהיא נפש, וקרינא ביה ״על כל נפשות מת לא יבא״:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:15:4.english: A person who has only one revi'it - For a person is sustained by a revi'it of blood. This measure is a halakha transmitted to Moses at Sinai: a revi'it of blood from a corpse imparts impurity in a tent, because it is [the] soul, and we read concerning it: "He shall not come near any dead soul" (Numbers 6:6).

Rashi on Sotah 5a:16:1.hebrew: אחד משמונה בשמינית - משקל קטן הוא, והיינו עוכלא. כלומר, צריך שיהיה בו מעט גאוה, שלא יהו קלי הראש מסתוללין בו, ויהא דבריו מתקבלין עליהן בעל כרחם:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:16:1.english: One part of eight in an eighth - It is a small measure of weight, that is, an *ukla*. That is to say, he must have a little pride, so that frivolous people will not treat him with contempt, and his words will be accepted by them even against their will.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:16:2.hebrew: ומעטרא ליה כי סאסא לשיבלתא - גסות מועט נאה והוגנת לו לתלמיד חכם, ומעטרתו כסאסא המעטרת את השבולת:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:16:2.english: And it adorns him like a thorn [adorns] the ear of grain - A little haughtiness is becoming and fitting for a Torah scholar, and it adorns him like the thorn that adorns the ear of grain.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:16:3.english: With the ban of excommunication that is in him - [Namely,] arrogance.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:16:4.hebrew: ובשמתא דלית ביה - גסות פורתא, לפי שאין בני עירו יראים ממנו, ואין בו כח להוכיחם:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:16:4.english: And [he is] under a ban, if he does not have in him - a little arrogance, because the people of his town do not fear him, and he has no power to rebuke them.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:17:1.hebrew: לא ממנה ולא ממקצתה - לא יחפוץ אדם לא בכולה ולא במקצתה, דמי זוטר מאי דקרי ליה קרא ״תועבת ה׳״:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:17:1.english: Neither from it nor from part of it - A person should not desire it, neither all of it nor any part of it, for even a small amount of that which the verse calls "an abomination of the Lord."

Rashi on Sotah 5a:18:1.english: Like flesh - For it is soft, and not like a stone, which is hard.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:18:2.hebrew: להשתחוות - להתפלל. אותם שהם בשר יבואו ויתפללו, כי הם נשמעים לפני; אבל גסי הרוח לא יבואו:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:18:2.english: To bow down - To pray. Those who are [like] flesh shall come and pray, for they are heard before Me; but the haughty shall not come.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:19:1.hebrew: בשר כתיב ביה ונרפא - ״ובשר כי יהיה בו בעורו שחין ונרפא״; ״אדם כי יהיה בעור בשרו נגע צרעת״; ״כי תהיה באדם״ — לא כתיב בחד מינייהו ״ונרפא״. לפי דרכך אתה למד, שמי שהוא רך ועניו כבשר, קרוב להתרפאות מיסורין הבאין עליו; אבל מי שהוא קשה כאדמה, אין רפואה למכותיו:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:19:1.english: With “flesh” it is written “and he is healed” - “And when the flesh has in its skin a boil, and it is healed”; “When a man has in the skin of his flesh a tzara'at affliction”; “When tzara'at is in a man” — in neither of these [last two] is “and he is healed” written. By your own reasoning, you can learn that one who is soft and humble like flesh is close to being healed from the suffering that comes upon him; but one who is hard like earth has no cure for his wounds.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:1:1.hebrew: אפילו עושה צדקה בסתר - שנותן מידו לידו של העני. והכי משמע: יד הנותנת ליד — אף הוא לא ינקה:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:1:1.english: Even one who gives charity in secret - Who gives from his hand into the hand of the poor person. And this is the meaning [of the verse]: a hand that gives to a hand — he too shall not go unpunished.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:1:2.hebrew: דכתיב ביה מתן בסתר כו' - לאו דשייך האי קרא בקרא דלעיל, אלא רבותא היא שאע"פ שמכפה אף וחימה, אינו מכפר על גסות הרוח:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:1:2.english: For it is written about it: "A gift in secret [subdues anger]" etc. - It is not that this verse is connected to the verse above; rather, it is a novelty: even though [a gift in secret] covers [i.e., subdues] anger and wrath, it does not atone for arrogance.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:20:1.hebrew: אדם - למה נקרא שמו אדם? שהוא אפר, דם, מרה. כלומר, כולו הבל, לכך אל יתגאה. מרה היא ליחלוחית מרה היוצאה מן המרירה שבכבד, ומתגברת באדם הכל לפי החדשים ושינוי העתים, ולפי המאכל שאוכל, ועל ידיה באין חליים ונגעים ומכאובות. יש שקורין בדברי הרופאים "מרירה שחורה", ויש שקורין "מרירה אדומה":
Rashi on Sotah 5a:20:1.english: Adam - Why is his name called Adam? Because he is *afar* (dust), *dam* (blood), *marah* (bile). That is to say, he is entirely futility; therefore, he should not be arrogant. *Marah* (bile) is the moisture of bile that emerges from the bitterness [i.e., the gall] in the liver, and it grows stronger in a person according to the months and the change of seasons, and according to the food that he eats; and through it, illnesses, afflictions, and pains come. In the words of the physicians, some call it "black bile," and some call it "red bile."

Rashi on Sotah 5a:20:2.english: Sheol - The place of Sheol is his house.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:21:1.hebrew: נפחת - מתמעט מחשיבותו, ונעשה פחות באנשים:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:21:1.english: He is diminished - He is reduced in his importance and becomes lesser among people.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:2:1.english: A warning - That one should not be haughty.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:2:2.hebrew: ורם לבבך ושכחת - אלמא מגובה לב בא לידי שכחה, ששוכח את בוראו, ובשכחה הוא מוזהר: "השמר לך פן תשכח":
Rashi on Sotah 5a:2:2.english: “And your heart will be lifted up, and you will forget” - Evidently, from haughtiness of heart one comes to forgetfulness, as he forgets his Creator; and with regard to forgetfulness he is warned: “Beware lest you forget.”

Rashi on Sotah 5a:4:2.english: His height is diminished - Since his height is diminished.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:4:3.english: He exists in the world - He endures.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:5:1.hebrew: והומכו - ואם חזר ונעשה עניו, שממיך את עצמו:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:5:1.english: And they are brought low - And if he repented and became humble, [one] who lowers himself.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:5:2.english: Like all - Like those regarding whom "all" is stated.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:5:3.hebrew: יקפצון - מן העולם ימותו מות ישרים. אברהם כתיב ביה "וה' ברך את אברהם בכל", יצחק כתיב ביה "ואוכל מכל", יעקב כתיב ביה "כי חנני אלהים וכי יש לי כל". והכי מפרש בהדיא בבראשית רבה (דבשלמא "בכל" "מכל" רבותא הוא שנתברכו בכל, אבל "וכל אשר תתן לי" מילתא בעלמא הוא דקאמר):
Rashi on Sotah 5a:5:3.english: They will be cut off - from the world; they will die the death of the upright. Of Abraham it is written, "And the Lord blessed Abraham with everything [bakol]"; of Isaac it is written, "And I ate of everything [mikol]"; of Jacob it is written, "For God has favored me, and I have everything [kol]." And this is explained explicitly in Bereshit Rabbah. (For it is indeed a distinction in the case of "with everything" and "of everything" that they were blessed with everything; but "and all that You give me" is merely a casual remark that [Jacob] made.)

Rashi on Sotah 5a:6:1.hebrew: כסאסא דשיבלתא - גבהו של שבולת, שקורין זקן השבולת, והוא נשבר ונופל מאליו:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:6:1.english: Like the *sasa* of the ear of grain - The tip of the ear of grain, which is called the beard of the ear, and it breaks off and falls by itself.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:6:2.hebrew: גבוהה גבוהה הוא מלקט - והיינו "וכראש שבולת", שראשה נראית למעלה מחברותיה:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:6:2.english: The high, the high one he gathers - And this is [the meaning of] "and like the head of an ear of grain," whose head is seen above its fellows.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:7:1.hebrew: אתי דכא - אני מגביהו עד ששוכן אצלי, והיינו ״אשכון את דכא״:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:7:1.english: With the contrite one - I raise him up until he dwells beside Me, and this is [the meaning of] "I will dwell with the contrite."

Rashi on Sotah 5a:7:2.english: I [am with] the crushed - I lower My Presence [Shekhinah] to be with him.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:9:1.hebrew: ילמד אדם מדעת קונו - לאהוב את הנמיכות:
Rashi on Sotah 5a:9:1.english: A person should learn from the mind of his Maker - To love humility.

Rashi on Sotah 5a:9:2.hebrew: כל הרים וגבעות - כגון תבור וכרמל, שבאו שם, כדכתיב: למה תרצדון הרים גבנונים (תהלים סח):
Rashi on Sotah 5a:9:2.english: All mountains and hills - For example, Tabor and Carmel, which came there, as it is written: "Why do you leap, you many-peaked mountains?" (Psalms 68).

Tosafot on Sotah 5a:11:1.hebrew: כל אדם שיש בו גסות הרוח אין עפרו ננער - תימה: אמאי לא חשיב האי במשנת חלק? והא דאמר פרק בתרא דכתובות (דף קיא.): מתים שבחו"ל אינן חיים; ותו גרסינן התם: ע"ה אינן חיים אא"כ יהנו תלמידי חכמים; ומלוי רביות מצינו באגדה שאינן חיים לעולם הבא. תוס' ר"י:
Tosafot on Sotah 5a:11:1.english: Any person who has arrogance in him, his dust is not shaken off - It is astonishing: Why does [the Mishnah] not count this one in the Mishnah of Chelek [Sanhedrin, ch. 10]? And [likewise] that which is stated in the last chapter of Ketubot (111a): The dead who are outside the Land [of Israel] will not come back to life; and furthermore we read there: Ignorant people will not come back to life unless they benefit Torah scholars; and as for lenders at interest, we find in the Aggadah that they will not live in the World to Come. Tosafot of R. Yitzchak.

Tosafot on Sotah 5a:15:1.hebrew: אדם שאין בו אלא רביעית דם - פר"ח: הוא דם הצלול שממנו משתית הלב; אין בו אלא משקל כ"ה סלעים, שהיא רביעית הלוג:
Tosafot on Sotah 5a:15:1.english: A person has only a quarter-log of blood - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: It is the clear blood from which the foundation of the heart [is formed]; it amounts to only the weight of twenty-five sela'im, which is a quarter of a log.
